Honestly, is the pricier one worth the extra, or is the cheaper one fine?
Whether the Polygon Tambora A4 is worth the extra $400 depends on how and where you plan to ride.
The Polygon Tambora G4 ($1,199.99) is perfectly fine if you want a reliable, budget-friendly ride for recreational gravel, light commuting, or flatter routes. Its 1x10 MicroSHIFT Advent X drivetrain keeps things simple and easy to maintain, but you'll have larger gaps between gears on steep inclines.
The Polygon Tambora A4 ($1,599.99) is worth the extra cost if you plan on riding steeper hills, longer distances, or competitive events. Upgrading to the Shimano GRX 2x11 group set provides a wider overall gear range with tighter, smoother shifts, making pedaling much more efficient over varied terrain.
If money is tight, the G4 offers exceptional value and gets you out on the trails without breaking the bank.
